blocks.text: Dohra:

There was one Singh known as Tara Singh1 (Gaiba), Who belonged the Khalsa Panth Misl of Dalewalia2 . There was also one Mit Singh (the rioteer in this Misl), Who arrived at an (independent) resolution of his own: (1)
lines: There was one Singh known as Tara Singh1 (Gaiba),
Who belonged the Khalsa Panth Misl of Dalewalia2 .
There was also one Mit Singh (the rioteer in this Misl),
Who arrived at an (independent) resolution of his own:

blocks.text: Chaupai:

That ten thousand Singhs, having an independent mind, They should raid across the Yamuna river the early morning. Overhearing this conversation did Tara Singh tell Mit Singh, That the latter alone was an egocentric among the Khalsa Panth. (2)
lines: That ten thousand Singhs, having an independent mind,
They should raid across the Yamuna river the early morning.
Overhearing this conversation did Tara Singh tell Mit Singh,
That the latter alone was an egocentric among the Khalsa Panth.

blocks.text: Warning him against crossing Yamuna with a smaller strength, He cautioned him against getting defeated and massacred. Reminding him about the Mughal troops stationed at Lahore, He must not consider Ahmad Shah Abdali's3 forces very far. (3)
lines: Warning him against crossing Yamuna with a smaller strength,
He cautioned him against getting defeated and massacred.
Reminding him about the Mughal troops stationed at Lahore,
He must not consider Ahmad Shah Abdali's3 forces very far.

blocks.text: Paying no heed to Tara Singh's advice and crossing Yamuna river, Mit Singh raided and ransacked Rohela's4 territories. Ahmad Shah Abdali beig a close ally of Ruhela, The latter did sent a messager to Ahmad Shah post hate. (4)
lines: Paying no heed to Tara Singh's advice and crossing Yamuna river,
Mit Singh raided and ransacked Rohela's4 territories.
Ahmad Shah Abdali beig a close ally of Ruhela,
The latter did sent a messager to Ahmad Shah post hate.

blocks.text: Ahmad Shah being already on the look out for the Singhs, Immediately did he despatch his troops at Rohela's bidding. Thus did the Afghan forces from Lahore and Sirhind arrive, Desperately in need as Najibuddin Rohela was of these forces. (5)
lines: Ahmad Shah being already on the look out for the Singhs,
Immediately did he despatch his troops at Rohela's bidding.
Thus did the Afghan forces from Lahore and Sirhind arrive,
Desperately in need as Najibuddin Rohela was of these forces.

blocks.text: For ten days did (Mit Singh's) contingent kept looting and plundering, Ransacking, most of the territory around the city of Meerut. Being neither aware nor concerned about any reprisals, The Singhs had no inkling about the arrival of Afghan troops. (6)
lines: For ten days did (Mit Singh's) contingent kept looting and plundering,
Ransacking, most of the territory around the city of Meerut.
Being neither aware nor concerned about any reprisals,
The Singhs had no inkling about the arrival of Afghan troops.

blocks.text: Dohra:

Thus, for days and nights did these troops keep assembling, Which consisted of troops of Rohela and Afghan troops of Abdali. With the break of the Sun's rays, did they attack as suddenly, As the waves that rise in a river in flood. (7)
lines: Thus, for days and nights did these troops keep assembling,
Which consisted of troops of Rohela and Afghan troops of Abdali.
With the break of the Sun's rays, did they attack as suddenly,
As the waves that rise in a river in flood.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Singhs' horses having been loaded with war booty, They temselves were carrying heavy loads on their backs, Thus did they feel harassed by this sudden attack, As they could not wield their armours with heavy loads. (8)
lines: Singhs' horses having been loaded with war booty,
They temselves were carrying heavy loads on their backs,
Thus did they feel harassed by this sudden attack,
As they could not wield their armours with heavy loads.

blocks.text: As the Singh felt like fleeing from the field of battle, They could not engage the enemy in a straight fight, Those among the Singhs who were of obstinate disposition, They perished in the fight as they could not resist the enemy. (9)
lines: As the Singh felt like fleeing from the field of battle,
They could not engage the enemy in a straight fight,
Those among the Singhs who were of obstinate disposition,
They perished in the fight as they could not resist the enemy.

blocks.text: Then did it dawn upon Mit Singh's mind so soon, The admonition that the veteran Singhs had earlier delivered him. As he kept on fighting hitting, running and hitting again, How could he fight single handed with those outnumbering him. As his horse fell down after being hit by a bullet, His own foot got entangled in the horse's stirrups. (10)
lines: Then did it dawn upon Mit Singh's mind so soon,
The admonition that the veteran Singhs had earlier delivered him.
As he kept on fighting hitting, running and hitting again,
How could he fight single handed with those outnumbering him.
As his horse fell down after being hit by a bullet,
His own foot got entangled in the horse's stirrups.

blocks.text: Dohra:
Those Singhs who had had mighty horses under them, They did keep fighting from the front and retreating.
Despite this running, hitting and running again and again, Five to six thousand Singhs perished in this skirmish. (11)
lines: Despite this running, hitting and running again and again,
Five to six thousand Singhs perished in this skirmish.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Thus did Afghan invaders win this victory gratuitously, Afghan commander Jahankhan5 getting the credit for it. Thus number of Singhs who got beheaded in this fight, They constituted a cargo of eighteen cartloads of Najabudin's baggage. (12)
lines: Thus did Afghan invaders win this victory gratuitously,
Afghan commander Jahankhan5 getting the credit for it.
Thus number of Singhs who got beheaded in this fight,
They constituted a cargo of eighteen cartloads of Najabudin's baggage.

blocks.text: Dohra:

As those loaded carts carrying a cargo of beheaded of Singh's heads, Put up a halt at a wayside inn on the banks of river Ghaggar, There did they hear several kinds of flying rumours, That large contingents of Singhs were about to attack. (13)
lines: As those loaded carts carrying a cargo of beheaded of Singh's heads,
Put up a halt at a wayside inn on the banks of river Ghaggar,
There did they hear several kinds of flying rumours,
That large contingents of Singhs were about to attack.

blocks.text: Chaupai:

Dumping the beheaded Singhs' heads at that spot, They ran back speedily with their empty carts. There resided two of Mit Singh's nephews in the vicinity, Who were known by the names of Bhag Singh and Bhanga Singh.6 (14)
lines: Dumping the beheaded Singhs' heads at that spot,
They ran back speedily with their empty carts.
There resided two of Mit Singh's nephews in the vicinity,
Who were known by the names of Bhag Singh and Bhanga Singh.6

blocks.text: They were those who had occupied the city of Thanesar, They were those who rushed to cremate the Singhs' heads. This halloed place came to be known as Shaheedganj , Where people made offerings for getting their wishes fulfilled. (15)
lines: They were those who had occupied the city of Thanesar,
They were those who rushed to cremate the Singhs' heads.
This halloed place came to be known as Shaheedganj ,
Where people made offerings for getting their wishes fulfilled.

blocks.text: Dohra:

This incident took place in the year eighteen hundred twently three7 , In the Bikrami Samvat of the Indian calendar. Mit Singh had made this supreme sacrifice in this way, As he had put up a brave fight with Jahan Khan's forces. (16)
lines: This incident took place in the year eighteen hundred twently three7 ,
In the Bikrami Samvat of the Indian calendar.
Mit Singh had made this supreme sacrifice in this way,
As he had put up a brave fight with Jahan Khan's forces.
